title: Notice a final silent e
goal: Use a taught spelling pattern to attempt a word, check its pronunciation and connect it with meaning.
cue: Compare cap and cape. The final e is not a separate spoken syllable; it often signals a different vowel earlier in the word. Listen and check exceptions in a dictionary.
spelling: A common pattern is a_e as in cape or i_e as in kite. It is a useful clue, not a rule for every word ending in e.

articulation.label: cap
articulation.alt: cap: /k/ → /æ/ → /p/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /k/: Back of tongue meets the soft palate; release.
/æ/: Low front tongue; open the jaw.
/p/: Close the lips, then release the air.
articulation.note: Join the sounds smoothly after practising each position.

articulation.label: cape
articulation.alt: cape: /k/ → /eɪ/ → /p/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /k/: Back of tongue meets the soft palate; release.
/e/: Start with the tongue mid-front.
/ɪ/: Raise the front tongue; narrow the jaw gap.
/p/: Close the lips, then release the air.
articulation.note: Keep each vowel glide inside one syllable.

articulation.label: kit
articulation.alt: kit: /k/ → /ɪ/ → /t/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /k/: Back of tongue meets the soft palate; release.
/ɪ/: Front tongue, a little lower and relaxed.
/t/: Tongue tip touches the ridge, then releases.
articulation.note: Join the sounds smoothly after practising each position.

articulation.label: kite
articulation.alt: kite: /k/ → /aɪ/ → /t/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /k/: Back of tongue meets the soft palate; release.
/a/: Start with the tongue low and jaw open.
/ɪ/: Glide up and forward; narrow the jaw gap.
/t/: Tongue tip touches the ridge, then releases.
articulation.note: Keep each vowel glide inside one syllable.

move something from a place or person. Puck is taking a cup from the table.
